messages.t:
I'm Detective Theo Marsh. I have parts of the investigation file. What I don't have is the complete wedding ledger. You do.

I've been going back through the evidence the original investigation used against Jasmine.

There's something bothering me about it.

The case against her is built around what she did before Margery died.

I'm interested in what happened after Margery left the reception.

Let's start with the evidence I can recover.

I went back through the CCTV report.

Most of the reception was covered, but there was a gap in the camera coverage. The report places the blind spot around Tables 46 through 50.

That's important, but it doesn't tell us who was there.

Check that section of the wedding ledger for me.

What count do you get?

That's still too many people.

I went back to the physical evidence.

There's a handwritten mark on one of the items recovered during the investigation. It's damaged, but I can make out what might be a first initial.

T, H, J, or I.

I'm not confident enough to say which one it is.

See what that does to the group.

What count do you get?

I also had the lab re-check something recovered from the reception.

They identified chicken gravy.

It may give us another way to narrow the same group.

Check the meal field.

What count do you get?

There's another part of the original investigation I want you to see before we continue with the ledger.

The detective who built the original case left behind a working suspect profile. I don't know whether the profile is correct, but it gives us somewhere to start.

Four things stand out:

First name: I–Q
Wedding side: Bride's side
Table: Odd-numbered
RSVP: Confirmed after the RSVP deadline

There is one person I want to test first. Ella Taylor is one of the names I want to examine.

Ella wasn't our killer. But her statement gives us something we didn't have before.

She saw the person heading toward the cellar wearing a pink guest badge.

I checked the reception records. The pink badge was assigned to the bride's side.

Check the remaining records for the bride's side.

What count do you get?

docs.title: ELLA TAYLOR — INTERROGATION REPORT
docs.body:
We interviewed Ella Taylor.

Ella denied killing Margery.

During the interview, however, she admitted that she had been near the reception area when Margery left.

Ella says she saw another person moving toward the cellar.

She couldn't identify the person.

But she remembers one detail clearly:

The person was wearing a pink guest badge.

Ella has been cleared as the person responsible for Margery's death.

progress.task: Check the remaining records for the bride's side. What count do you get?
